avalancheActivity.highlights: Wind slabs along the border between Valais and France.
avalancheActivity.comment:
On wind-loaded slopes and on extremely steep slopes dry avalanches are possible, even medium-sized ones. Above approximately 2300 m they can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers and reach large size in some cases. As the day progresses the likelihood of loose snow slides being released will increase in particular on rocky slopes. Individual gliding avalanches can also occur, in particular on steep grassy slopes.

New snow and wind slabs can in some cases be released by a single winter sport participant. This applies in particular on very steep slopes. They represent the main danger. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher.

snowpackStructure.comment:
In particular in the northwest 15 to 30 cm of snow fell on Wednesday above approximately 1200 m. Little snow will fall until Thursday in some localities.

As a consequence of the occasionally strong northerly wind, fresh snow drift accumulations will form on Thursday.
Above approximately 2200 m there are 70 to 140 cm of snow, and even as much as 190 cm in some localities, especially above approximately 2500 m.
The snowpack is not distinctly layered. The snowpack will be unstable in some places. Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

tendency.highlights: The weather conditions will facilitate a gradual strengthening of the snowpack. The danger will decrease gradually.

avalancheActivity.highlights: New snow and wind slabs are to be assessed with care and prudence.
avalancheActivity.comment:
20 to 30 cm of snow has fallen since yesterday above approximately 1600 m.
New snow and wind slabs can in some cases be released by a single winter sport participant. This applies in particular on very steep slopes.
As a consequence of new snow and wind the wind slabs will increase in size additionally as the day progresses. On wind-loaded slopes and on extremely steep slopes avalanches are possible, in particular medium-sized ones. Above approximately 2300 m they can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers and reach large size in some cases.

The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

snowpackStructure.comment: The sometimes moderate wind has transported the new snow. Faceted weak layers exist in the snowpack in particular in places that are protected from the wind. Below approximately 2000 m from a snow sport perspective, in most cases insufficient snow is lying, especially in the Prealps.

avalancheActivity.highlights: Over a wide area 50 cm of snow, and even more in some localities, will fall.
avalancheActivity.comment:
In steep rocky terrain and on very steep slopes small and medium sized avalanches are to be expected as the day progresses. Individual gliding avalanches can also occur.

The wind slabs can be released even by a single winter sport participant in all aspects above the tree line. They will be covered with new snow and therefore difficult to recognise. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher.

snowpackStructure.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and a moderate southerly wind, wind slabs will form adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls.
Below approximately 2000 m only a little snow is lying.
Towards its base, the snowpack is faceted and weak.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

tendency.highlights: Northerly wind. The danger will persist.

avalancheActivity.highlights: New snow and wind slabs at intermediate and high altitudes.
avalancheActivity.comment:
15 to 30 cm of snow, and even more in some localities, has fallen since yesterday above approximately 1500 m.
The new snow of yesterday is in some cases prone to triggering. As a consequence of new snow and wind the wind slabs will increase in size additionally as the day progresses.
In particular adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls medium-sized and, in isolated cases, large avalanches are possible. In addition the soft wind slabs are easily triggered.

The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

snowpackStructure.comment: The sometimes moderate wind has transported the new snow. Faceted weak layers exist in the snowpack in particular in places that are protected from the wind. Below approximately 2000 m from a snow sport perspective, in most cases insufficient snow is lying.

avalancheActivity.highlights: Little snow will fall until Thursday.
avalancheActivity.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and wind individual natural avalanches are possible as the day progresses. Mostly these are small. Above approximately 2300 m they can be released in the new snow and wind slab layers.

The wind slabs of the last few days can be released by a single winter sport participant in isolated cases.
Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher.

snowpackStructure.comment:
Over a wide area 15 to 20 cm of snow fell on Wednesday above approximately 1200 m. Little snow will fall until Thursday in some localities.
As a consequence of the strong northerly wind, fresh snow drift accumulations will form on Thursday.
Above approximately 2000 m there are 30 to 70 cm of snow, and even more in some localities.
The snowpack will be in some cases unstable.
Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.
At low and intermediate altitudes only a little snow is lying.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

tendency.highlights: The weather conditions will foster a gradual strengthening of the near-surface layers. The danger will persist.

regions.name: B - VALLI DI GRESSONEY, AYAS, CHAMPORCHER

avalancheActivity.highlights: New snow and wind slabs at intermediate and high altitudes.
avalancheActivity.comment:
15 to 20 cm of snow has fallen since yesterday above approximately 1500 m.
The new snow of yesterday is in some cases prone to triggering. The sometimes moderate wind has transported the new snow.
In particular adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls small and, in isolated cases, medium-sized avalanches are possible. In addition the soft wind slabs are capable of being triggered.

The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

snowpackStructure.comment: The new snow of yesterday is loosely bonded on shady slopes. As a consequence of solar radiation a crust will form on the surface in the course of the day. This applies in particular on sunny slopes.

avalancheActivity.comment: 15 to 25 cm of snow fell yesterday above approximately 1600 m. The avalanche prone locations are very rare. They are to be found on extremely steep shady slopes in high Alpine regions. Restraint should be exercised because avalanches can sweep people along and give rise to falls.
